payload.text: **THE FOUR COLLECTION ADDRESSES RESOLVE.** `intent:///threads`, `intent:///issues`, `intent:///threads/{stid}/wp` and `intent:///threads/{stid}/ac` parse and resolve in `address.rs`, and until this row **no criterion in this thread reached their resolution.** AC-07.1's population is *every ENTITY form in D57-8's list* and is faithful to that -- against nine entity forms it is satisfied and stays satisfied. **This is a new criterion rather than a widening of AC-07.1, on the discriminator this thread has used four times: what does satisfying the existing row completely still leave broken?** All nine entity forms resolving through one implementation leaves four addressable collection forms with no resolution coverage at all. **The four entered the grammar through D57-8's POST clause and its under-addressing clause while D57-8's own enumerating fence stayed at nine** (amended 2026-08-20), so they were mandated, implemented, and unreachable by any test that enumerates the grammar from the document. **Resolution is implemented ONCE for these as for the entity forms** -- the CLI and intentd call the same function in `intentsvcs` -- and the singularity arm is asserted structurally, as AC-07.1 requires, not by comparing two outputs.
